analyticalQuestion: After taking the soft positive part component by component, equivalently forming the componentwise relaxed positive-entry measure, which part of the R0.71P sum is paid by fixed spatial overlap, and which temporal quantity remains?
takeaway: The componentwise relaxed positive-entry measure is generally not the positive Jordan part of a signed aggregate. Bounded overlap closes simultaneous spatial batching, while distinct entry-time packing remains uncontrolled by the ordinary budgets tested here.
measureConvention: Take soft positive parts component by component before summing. Do not replace this measure by the positive Jordan part of a signed shell-cell aggregate.
nonColorEncoding: solid versus dashed and dotted lines

panels.A: segmented or soft positive entry versus ordinary hard positive jump
panels.C: sequential abstract entries versus ordinary time budgets
panels.D: sharp genuine NSE one-sided initial entry

claimBoundary: Panel C uses the half-open window [0,2*pi), includes the left endpoint, excludes the right endpoint, and has exactly N positive atoms. It is an abstract smooth Hilbert path, not a coupled NSE multiple-face construction. Panel D is one one-sided smooth NSE initial jet, not a time step or an internal or repeated NSE face theorem. No infinite-frame, Leray, continuation, singularity, regularity, originality, or Millennium-problem claim is shown.
